collection.title: Noemorph cross-cultural, historical, religious-philosophical, and Indigenous breadth additions
collection.method: Candidate construction from record-specific primary translations, peer-reviewed scholarship, institutional editions, community-authored frameworks, specialist encyclopedias, and exact-name/alias collision auditing against the registered Noemorph corpus.
collection.source_policy: Every record retains at least two HTTPS locators. DOI resolution and locator availability are recorded separately from interpretive review. Community-authored sources are preferred for living Indigenous frameworks; externally theorized ethnographic models are labeled as such.
collection.coverage_note: This provisional shard separates named traditions and thinkers instead of treating geographic regions as single theories. It includes South Asian, Buddhist, Sikh, Jaina, Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Arabic-Islamic, Jewish, African, Indigenous American, Pacific, and ancient religious-philosophical records. It is not exhaustive.
collection.translation_policy: Key non-English terms remain visible. English glosses are treated as provisional, polysemy and textual layers are noted per record, and no cross-tradition equivalence edges are asserted.
collection.community_and_ethnography_policy: Living Indigenous frameworks are bounded to named authors, communities, institutions, or public scholarship. External anthropological syntheses remain attributed to their theorists and are not presented as uniform community belief.
exclusions: Parent theories already represented in the merged corpus—including Advaita, Sāṃkhya–Yoga, Yogācāra, Madhyamaka, Dzogchen, Mahāmudrā, Pratyabhijñā, Tiantai, Huayan in Fazang, Wang Yangming, Akan, Yorùbá, and existing Māori/Ojibwe records—were not renamed and double-counted.
Generic pan-Indigenous medicine-wheel, animism, shamanism, chakra, and 'Eastern mind' headings were excluded because they collapse distinct communities or lack bounded attribution.
Restricted, initiatory, or community-controlled knowledge was not sought; only publicly available scholarship and institutional records were used.
Cross-cultural synthesis, equivalence claims, and graph relationships remain deferred until candidate review and identity resolution are complete.

records.name: Taittirīya Upaniṣad five-sheath model
records.tradition: Early Upaniṣadic thought and later Vedānta reception
records.status: historically foundational · interpretations diverge by Vedānta school
records.status_note: The fivefold sequence is textual; whether kośa means sheath, layer, or domain and how it relates to ātman differs across commentaries.
records.summary: The Taittirīya Upaniṣad describes the person through food, breath, mind, understanding, and bliss formations, proceeding inward toward an account of self and brahman. Later Vedānta authors systematized these as five kośas used to distinguish changing psycho-physical functions from the self.
records.era: late first millennium BCE; continuing reception
records.scope: A textual and commentarial model of bodily, vital, mental, cognitive, and bliss-associated aspects of a person.
records.boundary_note: Kośa is a contested translation and does not denote five anatomical bodies or empirically separable neural levels. Later Advaita readings must not be projected back as the only meaning of the early text.
